headline: Gold prices jump: 22K gold now ৳2,24,940 per bhori after ৳6,590 hike
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has increased gold and silver prices due to a rise in the local market value of pure gold.
details: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has increased the price of 22-carat gold by ৳6,590 per bhori, setting the new price at ৳2,24,940.
According to a notice issued on Saturday (June 13), the new rates became effective from 10:00 AM. The hike is attributed to the increased price of pure gold in the local market.
Other rates include 21-carat gold at ৳2,14,734, 18-carat gold at ৳1,84,058, and traditional method gold at ৳1,49,882 per bhori.
This follows a previous adjustment on June 11, where prices were decreased by ৳4,432, bringing 22-carat gold down to ৳2,18,350.
So far this year, gold prices have been adjusted 74 times in the domestic market, with 38 increases and 36 decreases.
Silver prices have also risen by ৳291 per bhori, with 22-carat silver now priced at ৳5,132.
caption:
Gold prices in Bangladesh take a massive leap! 22K gold is now ৳2,24,940 per bhori.

The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has increased the price of 22-carat gold by ৳6,590 per bhori, setting the new price at ৳2,24,940.

According to a notice issued on Saturday (June 13), the new rates became effective from 10:00 AM. The hike is attributed to the increased price of pure gold in the local market.

Other rates include 21-carat gold at ৳2,14,734, 18-carat gold at ৳1,84,058, and traditional method gold at ৳1,49,882 per bhori.

This follows a previous adjustment on June 11, where prices were decreased by ৳4,432, bringing 22-carat gold down to ৳2,18,350.

So far this year, gold prices have been adjusted 74 times in the domestic market, with 38 increases and 36 decreases.

Silver prices have also risen by ৳291 per bhori, with 22-carat silver now priced at ৳5,132.

headline_marked: US police probe after [[England training equipment stolen]] in Kansas City
headline: US police probe after England training equipment stolen in Kansas City
summary: Balls and boots were among the items taken from vehicles transferring gear to the squad's training base ahead of their World Cup campaign.
details: England's World Cup preparations faced an unexpected setback when equipment was stolen from vehicles heading to their Kansas City training base on Saturday.
Items including footballs and boots were reportedly taken after the vehicles were broken into before arriving at the Swope Soccer Village base.
The Kansas City, Missouri Police Department confirmed they are investigating the theft, and the BBC reports that two arrests have already been made in connection with the incident.
The Football Association acknowledged the event but stated they could not provide further details as the matter is now under police investigation.
Thomas Tuchel's squad had transferred from their pre-tournament base in Florida and were scheduled to begin training in Kansas City at 5:00 pm on Saturday.
England is set to open their World Cup campaign against Croatia this Wednesday, followed by Group L matches against Ghana and Panama.
caption:
Imagine arriving for World Cup training only to find your boots and balls gone. That's exactly what happened to England.

England's World Cup preparations faced an unexpected setback when equipment was stolen from vehicles heading to their Kansas City training base on Saturday.

Items including footballs and boots were reportedly taken after the vehicles were broken into before arriving at the Swope Soccer Village base.

The Kansas City, Missouri Police Department confirmed they are investigating the theft, and the BBC reports that two arrests have already been made in connection with the incident.

The Football Association acknowledged the event but stated they could not provide further details as the matter is now under police investigation.

Thomas Tuchel's squad had transferred from their pre-tournament base in Florida and were scheduled to begin training in Kansas City at 5:00 pm on Saturday.

England is set to open their World Cup campaign against Croatia this Wednesday, followed by Group L matches against Ghana and Panama.
